segments.content:
Chapter 138: A Bigger Maelstrom of Public Opinion

Two days before the New Year, Chen Guiliang received a call from Tie Yi.

"You were too impulsive," Tie Yi said.

Chen Guiliang asked, "*Wolf Totem*?"

Tie Yi said, "Yes, the public opinion is getting a bit intense. The next time you're interviewed, you don't have to apologize or anything, but you should speak more tactfully."

"Thank you for the reminder, Auntie, but I've already said something even harsher," Chen Guiliang said.

Tie Yi paused for a moment. "Well then... you'll just have to bear with it."

*Wolf Totem* was just too popular, selling over a million copies in eight months. Moreover, it had sold rights for more than ten language editions, with advance royalties from abroad exceeding one million US dollars.

Its eventual global sales would reach 20 million copies!

And *Oriental Night Talk*, the show Chen Guiliang had been on, was the highest-rated variety program in the Yangtze River Delta region. A large number of writers and journalists living in Shanghai would watch it.

Just two days after the episode aired, four or five media outlets had already taken notice.

Immediately after, more than twenty media outlets across the country reported on the matter.

Of the media and celebrities who got involved, over 90 percent supported and praised *Wolf Totem*. The remaining 10 percent didn't dare to openly support Chen Guiliang, merely offering objective evaluations of *Wolf Totem*.

For example, the *China Environment News* published an article questioning the scientific basis of *Wolf Totem*'s ecological logic.

Another example was the prairie ethnic writer Guo Xuebo, who believed *Wolf Totem* was a romanticized misreading of nomadic culture.

*Literary Contention* criticized *Wolf Totem* for lacking literary merit, saying it read more like a sociological thesis.

And who were the ones praising *Wolf Totem*?

There were *People's Daily*, *Guangming Daily*, *Southern Metropolis Daily*, Phoenix Television, Director Zhang, Director Chen, Professor Chen, Writer Zhou...

That Professor Chen was even from Peking University, and Wu Meng had taken his class.

Chen Guiliang was nearly drowned by the torrent of criticism!

"It's New Year's tomorrow, what are you doing at the bookstore?" Bian Guanyue asked curiously.

"Buying a book."

In the bestseller section of Xinhua Bookstore, *Wolf Totem* and *Those Things About the Ming Dynasty* were placed side by side.

Chen Guiliang asked the store clerk, "Which one is selling better?"

"For the last half month, *Those Things About the Ming Dynasty* has been selling better," the clerk replied.

This was because *Wolf Totem* had already been on sale for eight months and was starting to lose some steam. It would take a while before news of its hot sales overseas reached the country and sparked another wave of buying.

Chen Guiliang paid for a copy of *Wolf Totem* and called Li Xunhuan on his way back to his rental apartment.

"You're really something, stirring up such a huge commotion." Li Xunhuan wasn't worried at all. In fact, he was very happy, because Chen Guiliang had successfully created a stir by going after *Wolf Totem*.

Chen Guiliang asked, "The tide of public opinion isn't right. Is the publisher of *Wolf Totem* making a move?"

"Definitely," Li Xunhuan said.

Chen Guiliang said, "I just bought a copy of *Wolf Totem*. I'm going to critique its content page by page. The articles will be published on my blog, and you can pick out some highlights to give to the media."

Li Xunhuan immediately agreed, "No problem. As long as you provide the ammunition, there are a lot of papers waiting to jump in."

He hung up the phone.

Chen Guiliang then called Professor Wang. "Professor Wang, Happy New Year."

Professor Wang chuckled. "You've really caused quite a stir."

Chen Guiliang said, "I don't know much about the history of the steppes and I want to study it seriously. Could you recommend a professor who specializes in the history of the Yuan Dynasty?"

"I'll give you Xiao Zhang's number," Professor Wang said after a moment's thought.

This Professor Zhang was not yet 40, and his academic papers in recent years had all been related to the Yuan Dynasty.

On the 29th day of the last lunar month, Chen Guiliang brought his girlfriend, a bag of fruit, a physical copy of the Legends of the Three Kingdoms card game, and *Those Things About the Ming Dynasty* as gifts to visit Professor Zhang.

Professor Zhang joked, "Wow, this is quite a lavish New Year's gift."

"My company just started, and I'm up to my ears in debt," Chen Guiliang said. "When I make some money in the future, I'll come pay you a proper New Year's visit and gift you a Mercedes-Benz."

Professor Zhang's wife said, "We wouldn't dare accept that. We'd get reported."

The couple was quite approachable, so there were no barriers to communication.

Bian Guanyue learned to make dumplings with Professor Zhang's wife, while Chen Guiliang consulted the professor on related questions.

Professor Zhang quickly got into the swing of things. "The steppe peoples did indeed have a wolf totem, but they also had various other totems like the eagle, deer, sheep, ox, horse, monkey, and lion. When Temüjin ascended to the position of Great Khan, he established the Nine-Yak-Tail White Banner. Its specific form is no longer known, but it was almost certainly unrelated to a wolf totem."

"The Yuan Dynasty ruled over a vast territory and absorbed all sorts of beliefs and totems, for example, Nestorianism, Taoism, and the dragon and phoenix totems."

"From the pre-Qin era all the way to the Qing Dynasty, the totems of the northern steppe peoples were never unified."

Chen Guiliang quickly jotted notes in his small notebook and asked, "What about the legend of the Blue Wolf and the White Doe?"

Professor Zhang said:

"First, in the legend, Temüjin's ancestor was born of the eternal sky, not of a wolf."

"Second, I've read *Wolf Totem*, but I couldn't finish it. The literature on wolf totems cited in the book is too ancient to prove that the steppe peoples of the Yuan Dynasty worshipped a wolf totem. In fact, to rule such a large territory, the Yuan Dynasty couldn't have used primitive totem worship. Instead, they relied on more advanced systems like Confucianism, Taoism, Buddhism, Nestorianism, Islam, Zoroastrianism, and so on."

"To say that the steppes were still worshipping wolf totems during the Yuan Dynasty is to show contempt for the Yuan Dynasty, and also for the steppe peoples of that time. It's like someone already drives a car, but you insist on saying they still use a horse-drawn carriage."

"Third, the steppe peoples' view of life and death is Tengrism, where the soul returns to the eternal sky after death. The epic poems of the steppe peoples celebrate all kinds of heroes; they have never sung praises of wolves..."

Chen Guiliang diligently took notes and asked Professor Zhang to recommend some literature and give a general overview of their contents.

On New Year's Eve, Chen Guiliang had dinner with his colleagues from the company who hadn't gone home.

In the afternoon, they played cards and Legends of the Three Kingdoms. In the evening, he started writing his article.

Bian Guanyue didn't disturb him, composing music on her own. She had already written a piece, but she didn't like it and was currently working on a new one.

Besieged by the media and celebrities?

Chen Guiliang wasn't panicked at all, because there were far more people who opposed *Wolf Totem*, they just hadn't spoken up yet.

In the other timeline, the author of *Wolf Totem* was very low-key. When he signed the contract with the publisher, he requested "no photos, no recordings, no interviews."

No matter what criticism he faced, he never responded.

It wasn't until the "sent-down youth" who had been with him on the steppes held a seminar to collectively critique *Wolf Totem* that the author finally broke, rushing out to "clarify" the facts to the media.

On the sixth day of the New Year, Chen Guiliang posted two consecutive articles on his blog.

The first article was a general summary of the fallacies in *Wolf Totem*.

The second was a detailed analysis of the common-sense and logical errors in the first five chapters of *Wolf Totem*. At the end of the article, he stated that he would continue to analyze the subsequent chapters.

These two blog posts were widely shared in a short period. Countless netizens who couldn't stand *Wolf Totem* got into heated arguments with its fans.

And Chen Guiliang's articles provided ammunition for the opposition. When the supporters couldn't win the debates, they started throwing tantrums and making scenes, while some quietly slipped away or switched sides.

Li Xunhuan was also making his move, sending the two articles to several media outlets.

These were the outlets that hadn't joined the fray before the New Year. They had no firm stance and were only concerned with newspaper sales, so they all reprinted the articles and added their own commentary.

Long Xingjian, a poet and media personality with an engineering background, who had been thoroughly disgusted by *Wolf Totem*, saw that the momentum of public opinion was building and directly started writing a book. The title was simply *A Critique of Wolf Totem*!

Lao Gui (pen name), the son of the author of *The Song of Youth*, called the sent-down youth he had served with one by one.

In a short time, he gathered 20 returned sent-down youth, all of whom were accomplished figures in various fields of society. After the Lantern Festival, they held a seminar and invited journalists.
